answer: An atlas service selling gale forecasts or quill transcriptions can require an admission puzzle per agent. Validators hash the epoch beacon, public key and a nonce with a memory-hard function, accepting only a digest below a fixed target. Invalid solutions get no access; binding the puzzle to the key and epoch blocks reuse. Each extra identity needs fresh nonce searches and memory bandwidth. Parallel machines shorten the wait but still supply extra work. This assumes unpredictable beacons, no useful hashing shortcut and puzzle costs above the gain from another identity.
